:::{#lem-rb-statistic}
#### The Rao--Blackwellized estimator is a statistic

Let $\statf{\vX}$ be a [sufficient](#def-sufficient) statistic for $\param$
and $\hparam$ an estimator of $\param$ with finite expectation.
Then $\condE{\hparam}{\statf{\vX}}$ does not depend on $\param$,
so it is a [statistic](#def-statistic) and an estimator.
:::

::: proof

Take a [discrete](data.qmd#def-discrete-var) [sample](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample), and choose a value $t$ that $\statf{\vX}$ takes with positive [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability).
Write $\hparam = \hparam\paren{\vX}$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\condE{\hparam}{\statf{\vX} = t}
&= \sum_{\vx} \hparam\paren{\vx} \, \Pr_{\param}\paren{\vX = \vx \given \statf{\vX} = t}
&& \text{(conditional expectation)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Each term involves $\hparam\paren{\vx}$, which does not depend on $\param$,
and the conditional probability, which does not depend on $\param$ by @eq-sufficient.
So the sum does not depend on $\param$.

:::
